change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The driver torque response time limit for accelerator pedal demand above 70% was reduced from 100 ms to 80 ms, requiring stricter timing limits in verification procedures and fresh execution where evidence exceeds 80 ms.

assessments.reason: TV-001 directly tests VCU-DR-01 response time. The requirement threshold tightened from 100 ms to 80 ms, making the current procedure limit of 100 ms obsolete and invalidating the previous PASS evidence of 94 ms.
evidence: Requirement VCU-DR-01 limit tightened from 100 ms to 80 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Update the test procedure threshold to 80 ms and rerun the test.

assessments.reason: TV-002 links to VCU-DR-01 and applies 85% pedal demand. Because previous evidence did not report measured response timing, rerun is needed to capture evidence against the 80 ms limit.
evidence: Comment notes timing not reported in old evidence
assessments.recommended_action: Rerun TV-002 and capture measured torque response time to verify compliance with the 80 ms limit.

assessments.reason: TV-003 measures high-load demand sweeps (75-95% pedal) and directly exercises VCU-DR-01 behavior despite a missing hyperlink. The previous result of 92 ms and script threshold of 95 ms do not meet the new 80 ms limit.
evidence: Comment notes legacy suite checks 95 ms tolerance
Workshop note confirms high-load campaign requirement links were lost
assessments.recommended_action: Update the procedure tolerance from 95 ms to 80 ms and rerun the test.

assessments.reason: TV-004 verifies emergency brake command latency under VCU-BRK-03. Workshop notes explicitly clarify that brake command latency uses a different measurement clock from driver torque response and must not be conflated.
evidence: Workshop note confirms brake latency and positive torque latency use different clocks

assessments.reason: TV-005 verifies wheel-speed sensor degradation mode and diagnostic logging under VCU-DGN-04, which remains unchanged.
TV-006 verifies audit logging of operating mode transitions under VCU-LOG-05, which is unchanged.
TV-007 applies 80% pedal demand which touches VCU-DR-01 behavior, but its requirement reference is TBD, the test was never run, and ownership is unclarified.
evidence: Comment notes ownership and source link to be clarified
assessments.recommended_action: Assign an engineering owner to clarify requirement mapping to VCU-DR-01 and define test criteria.

assessments.reason: TV-008 is a legacy diagnostic trace replay test unrelated to driver torque response time.
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for VCU-DR-01 change.

assessments.reason: TV-009 evaluates mode torque ramp profiles under VCU-MOD-06. While it indirectly exercises accelerator pedal response, it contains no quantitative timing assertion.
evidence: Comment notes no quantitative response-time assertion
assessments.recommended_action: Review whether TV-009 should include a quantitative response time limit aligned with VCU-DR-01.

assessments.reason: TV-010 tests pedal signal spike filtering under VCU-DR-02 (< 10 ms transient), which is unchanged.
evidence: Comment notes pedal sampling test only

assessments.reason: TV-011 tests emergency brake priority over propulsion torque under VCU-BRK-03, which is unchanged.
TV-012 measures ECU power cycle wake-up readiness timing, which is entirely independent of driver torque response.
